Yes. When a CIVIC alert is issued for a zone and you are a covered merchant in that zone, we check the area sales index every hour. If each of the last 3 hourly indices is below 50%, and the index for the whole 3 hours is also below the zone's lower bound from the forecasting model, the area income loss claim is triggered automatically. You are paid half your expected day's sales × the drop percentage, up to a daily cap of ₹2,500 per merchant.

Chhatri does not pay for income loss due to personal reasons like a family wedding or shop closure. We only cover area income loss (triggered by RAIN or CIVIC alerts and sales drops) or hospital-cash income loss.

The policy engine decides your claim automatically. When an area trigger fires, it checks if you have cover, your waiting period has ended, and your premium is paid. For hospital-cash claims, it checks the slip name, dates, readability, and number of days. If a slip check fails or is unsure, a claims officer reviews it.

If you disagree with a payout, tell us in the chat what you think we got wrong. A case opens and you see "Sent to a claims officer" with the case number, and we tell you that you will hear back within 24 hours. A claims officer checks the decision's numbers against the rules and either confirms the payout or rejects the dispute. If you are still unhappy, you can escalate to the insurer's grievance officer, then to IRDAI's Bima Bharosa portal, and finally to the Insurance Ombudsman.
